title: UNESCO AI Ethics Readiness Assessment Methodology 2026 — Crosswalk to Measurement Credentials
context: 2026-08-29 — UNESCO RAM 2.0 published; 50+ countries now require RAM-aligned AI system assessments
body: UNESCO's Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) 2.0, published August 2026, provides a structured framework for countries to assess their AI governance maturity across 12 dimensions including ethical oversight, transparency, accountability, and human oversight. For AI system operators serving governments that have adopted RAM, the methodology requires demonstrable measurement evidence — not policy documents, not self-attestations. The Council of AI measurement board maps to RAM dimensions as follows: (1) Ethical Oversight (Dimension 3) → Care axis + Governance axis signed credentials. (2) Transparency and Explainability (Dimension 5) → Detector-interoperability axis + Cross-reality axis. (3) Accountability (Dimension 6) → Machine-verifiability axis + signed manifest chain. (4) Human Oversight (Dimension 8) → Art-5 compliance measurement + privacy axis. Each Council of AI signed credential carries an Ed25519 signature verifiable against the published key — meeting RAM's requirement for independently verifiable evidence. Countries currently requiring RAM-aligned assessments include: Brazil, Chile, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Singapore, UAE, and EU member states (via UNESCO-EU joint programme).
references: UNESCO: Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021, adopted by 193 member states)
